chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nasri, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: We prayed Maghrib, then the Imam erred and gave salām after two rak'ahs, so we repeated the salat. He said: “Why did you repeat it? Did not the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم once depart after two rak'ahs and then complete it with two rak'ahs? Why did you not complete it?”

So there is nothing in these two reports that contradicts what we stated earlier, because the oversight here only occurred in that he gave salām in the second rak'ah, and the oversight had not occurred in the number of the salat. Whoever errs in the salām is not required to repeat the salat; rather, he must make it up with one rak'ah, according to what the two reports indicate. But if the oversight had occurred in the number, then repeating the salat from its beginning would have been obligatory, according to what we stated earlier. What clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَعْدَادِ: the numerical count of the units of prayer
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the salām that marks the apparent ending of the salat
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rak'ahs after which the Imam mistakenly ended the prayer
key_terms.السَّهْوَ: forgetfulness or inadvertent error occurring during salat
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.جُبْرَانُهُ: making up or compensating for the deficiency in the salat

ai.seo_question: If an Imam mistakenly ends Maghrib prayer after two rak'ahs, should the salat be repeated or completed?
ai.summary: This report discusses a ruling on forgetfulness in salat, specifically when the Imam gives salām after two rak'ahs in Maghrib prayer. The text explains that such an error in salām does not require repeating the entire salat; rather, it is remedied by completing the missing rak'ah, unlike an error in the actual count of rak'ahs, which would require repetition.
